headline.purpose: The hero only, plus the closing contact line. One per page.

title.purpose: Sub-heads inside a section list; the brief card title.

body.purpose: All running prose, capped at a 68ch measure.

label.purpose: Wide-tracked uppercase mono micro-label for data keys, speaker attributions and disclaimers. Never an eyebrow above a headline.

data.purpose: Short machine-flavoured values: brief fields, extracted facts, ordinals.

script.purpose: A patient utterance set in its own Indic face with lang set.

shadows.name: lifted-sheet
shadows.purpose: A paper card lifted off an ink-toned sheet. The brief card, and nothing else at this weight.

shadows.name: resting-sheet
shadows.purpose: A paper card resting on open water rather than lifted off a dark ground.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The system curve. Settle reveals, pill press, ripple-mark scale. The built-in easings read as unintentional.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Declared in the theme for symmetric in-out moves; not yet used by any built surface.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The page's one authored reveal. Additive only: released under .js plus prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, staggered 45-120ms between siblings.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Pill press. Physical response instead of a colour flash.

motion.name: tint
motion.value: background-color 220ms ease, color 220ms ease, border-color 220ms ease
motion.purpose: Pill hover ink-fill toward Wet Current.

motion.name: nav-land
motion.purpose: The nav landing on paper past 72% of viewport height: 88% paper ground, 10px backdrop blur, hairline base.

narrative.overview:
The whole page is one basin of water with ink floating on it, and the content is paper laid on the surface. A single WebGL fluid simulation is fixed behind every section; sheets of washi — three tones of it — scroll over the top, and the gaps between the sheets are where the water shows through. The ink is not decoration bolted to a hero: it is the ground the site is built on, and it stays live for the whole scroll. The metaphor is load-bearing rather than ornamental — the call is ink dropped in water, the doctor's brief is the sheet lifted off it.

The mood is quiet, cool and hand-made. Nothing glows. The fluid display pass composites subtractively over paper white with a Beer–Lambert coverage curve, so ink darkens the water the way ink actually does; there is no additive bloom anywhere in the system, in the shader or in the CSS. Type is held to one weight, one metric ramp, and a left margin. Where a sheet has to end, it tears rather than rounds: deckled edges rendered through an SVG turbulence-displacement filter. The result is dense with material but very low on chrome — no cards-with-icons, no gradient panels, no glass.

The build refuses the AI-health hero explicitly and completely: no dark gradient, no glowing waveform, no tilted dashboard mockup, no logo row, no product screenshot in perspective. It also refuses government-adjacent visual language — no national colours, no emblem-style mark — because the product must never read as state-affiliated. The single mark is a drawn ripple: the concentric rings one drop leaves on still water.
keyCharacteristics: One live WebGL ink basin fixed behind the entire page; content sheets scroll over it
Cool paper white and indigo — never cream, never warm
Torn deckled sheet edges instead of corner radii; pills are the only round form
One type weight (400), one display metric, hairline rules, wide-tracked mono micro-labels
Ink is subtractive: colour arrives by darkening, never by glowing
Nine real Indic script faces, because the scripts are the product's argument
Content visible by default; motion is additive and opt-out-aware

rules.name: The Dilute Line Rule
rules.body: --color-dilute draws lines and only lines. It fails text contrast on paper (3.3:1). Any text you were about to paint dilute takes --color-quiet (6.1:1) instead. No exceptions, including 11px labels.

rules.name: The Subtractive Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this world glows. Ink darkens paper; the display shader mixes toward the dye's own hue over the paper constant with 1 - exp(-a * 3.2) coverage, and the interface follows the same physics — no additive blends, no bloom, no light-on-dark gradient, no coloured glow behind anything.

rules.name: The Mixed-Ink Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is not its own token. On paper grounds it is color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-depth) 72–88%, var(--color-dilute)); on ink grounds it is color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-paper) 55–74%, var(--color-current)). Mixing from the ground's own ink keeps every tint inside the basin's family instead of introducing greys.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: The page uses a single weight. Nothing is bold — there is not one weight utility in the entire component tree — and font-synthesis-weight: none forbids the browser from faking one. Hierarchy comes from size, colour and space. The only exception is the mono micro-label at 500, which needs it to hold at 11px.

rules.name: The Endonym Rule
rules.body: A language is written in its own script, in a real face for that script, with lang set on the element. Never transliterate, never substitute a fallback stack, never show a language name in Latin only. The nine script faces are preload: false so the basin still paints first.

rules.name: The Mono Is Annotation Rule
rules.body: Azeret Mono never sets a sentence. It appears as a wide-tracked uppercase micro-label or as a short machine-flavoured value, and nowhere else.

rules.name: The One Basin Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one canvas, fixed behind everything, owned by a single module-scope handle. Sections do not get their own backgrounds, videos, or gradients-as-atmosphere; if a section wants ink, it drops ink into the shared basin. The canvas never takes pointer events — stirring is bound to window — so scrolling and every control above it behave normally.

rules.name: The Water Gap Rule
rules.body: The space between two sheets is the design, not padding that got away. Never close a gap by making adjacent sheets contiguous; the water has to show through.

rules.name: The Paper Wash Rule
rules.body: Where type must sit over live water, put a paper-tinted linear gradient underneath it (color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-paper) 30–95%, transparent), pointer-events-none, direction chosen to leave the ink visible). Never a blur, never a dark scrim, never a solid box.

rules.name: The Additive Reveal Rule
rules.body: Content renders visible. .settle sets opacity: 1; transform: none at baseline; the hidden state exists only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) scoped to .js on the document element. Nothing is ever gated behind a script that might not run, and reduced-motion users get the settled state immediately.

rules.name: The Deckle Layer Rule
rules.body: Deckled edges are separate absolutely-positioned <span> layers (104% wide, 26px tall, offset −13px, aria-hidden) that inherit the sheet's own ground through --sheet-bg and carry filter: url(#deckle). They are never pseudo-elements on the sheet itself and never wrap content, so the turbulence-displacement filter can never touch live text. A dark sheet tears dark because the layer reads the sheet's own background variable.

rules.name: The Lift-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this sheet is off the one behind it". Shadows are never used for hover feedback, never for buttons, never for inputs, and never as a hard offset. If nothing is lifted, nothing casts.

rules.name: The Torn Edge Rule
rules.body: Where a sheet ends, it tears. Do not introduce a corner radius on a sheet, card, or panel to soften it — the deckle is the softening. Radius belongs to pills and dots only.

dos: Do use --color-quiet (#4C5A70) for any small or secondary text; reserve --color-dilute (#7A8698) for lines, borders and dividers only.
Do build secondary tints with color-mix from the ground's own ink — depth-toward-dilute on paper, paper-toward-current on ink — instead of adding new grey tokens.
Do let the water show between sheets. A section that needs atmosphere becomes a transparent section with a paper wash, not a new background colour.
Do render deckle edges as separate aria-hidden layers that read --sheet-bg, so the displacement filter never touches text.
Do ship content visible and add motion on top: baseline .settle is settled, and the hidden state lives only inside .js plus prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
Do set every Indic string in its own Noto face with a lang attribute, and keep those faces preload: false.
Do gate hover treatments behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
Do keep one type weight and express hierarchy through size, colour and space.
Do draw icons as inline SVG in currentColor at a 1.15–1.3 stroke.
Do mark unresolved or uncertain information up, in Wet Current, rather than burying it.
donts: Don't set text in --color-dilute. It is 3.3:1 on paper and will fail at any size.
Don't add glow, bloom, additive blending, or a dark-gradient hero. Ink darkens; it never emits.
Don't put a corner radius on a sheet, card or panel. The edge language is the tear; radius belongs to pills and dots.
Don't use shadow for hover, buttons, inputs, or emphasis — only for a sheet genuinely lifted off another sheet, and never as a hard offset.
Don't add a second canvas or a per-section background animation. One basin, shared, with sections dropping ink into it.
Don't introduce a bold weight or a third family. Two Latin families plus the script faces is the whole program.
Don't apply the #deckle filter to any element containing live text.
Don't rely on Tailwind's text-current / border-current utilities: this theme defines a colour token literally named current (#243A63), which shadows them. Set the colour explicitly.
Don't use warm paper, cream, or a national-colour palette; the ground is cool white and the world must never read as state-affiliated.
Don't reach for a glyph icon, an emoji, or an icon font in place of the drawn ripple mark and arrow.
